applies_why: The judge text evaluates a collision between descent according to the flesh and conception of the Holy Ghost, which is the chain-against-chain situation K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; ... the stating-verse test DG-61 retires — one reading weighs the support of each chain without requiring an explicit verse resolving paternity; the other reading makes paternity underdetermined when the text lacks an explicit resolution.
why: The judge treats the absence of an explicit textual resolution of paternity as underdetermined, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than weighing the chains by footing.
